# Publish and maintain linked presentations

A linked presentation is a signed presentation of one credential, served at a URL and declared in your DID Document. It is how the public credentials of a service become visible. The agent manages them; this page explains what it does so you can read your DID Document.

## What is published

- Every ECS credential the agent holds (Service, Organization or Persona), under the reserved fragments `#vpr-schemas-service-vtc-vp`, `#vpr-schemas-org-vtc-vp`, `#vpr-schemas-persona-vtc-vp`.
- Every credential received through a flow, under a fragment of the form `#vpr-schemas-<qualifier>-vtc-vp`.
- For an ecosystem anchor, the schema credential of each schema, `#vpr-schemas-<qualifier>-vtjsc-vp`.
- With `did:webvh`, the Service credential is additionally exposed under the method's `#whois` entry, in addition to the required one.

## How it is maintained

| Event | Action |
|---|---|
| New credential | Entry added, DID Document republished, re-resolution triggered |
| Updated credential (renewal, validator update) | Entry replaced |
| Revocation of the credential or of the accreditation behind it | Entry removed, credential deleted |
| Change of a claim resource (logo, terms) | Nothing automatic: the credential still carries the old digest; obtain a new credential |

## Read your document

```bash
curl -s https://agent.example.com/.well-known/did.json | jq '.service[] | select(.type=="LinkedVerifiablePresentation") | {id, serviceEndpoint}'
```

Each endpoint returns a JSON presentation holding the credential. Verifiers fetch them during trust resolution.
